where: The Mirelights (the Glassmere: a drowned causeway-field of wandering false blue lights over a still mere)
mood: Eerie but tender: false blue lights drifting over still water, the echoes of a lost kin-light that once led travellers home.
_motif_note: Low-strength motif on purpose: the lost light used to lead people home, so the home tune sits faintly under the cue. Written at 90 BPM because the motif pins the take to its ~90 BPM grid.
_stall_note: deliberately sparse cue: a held hush between the lights is part of it (dead_air.py allows up to max_stall)
core_styles: 16-bit console RPG soundtrack from the mid-1990s
retro sampled-chip instruments with the warm echo of a 16-bit sound chip
3/4 time, a slow lilting waltz pulse
B minor with drifting whole-tone colour
a lone soft pulse-wave lead with long held notes and wide spacing
wandering high glass bells and celesta that drift slightly out of key like will-o'-the-wisps
a low still bass note under each bar
eerie but tender, a drowned field of blue lights over still water at night

sections.name: Intro
sections.text: {a lone glass bell light appears over the water, then a second answers slightly off key, and a low bass note settles under them}

sections.name: Main Theme
sections.text: {a lone pulse-wave lantern call in slow 3/4: a rising leap that hangs unresolved, wide rests between phrases, bells drifting off the beat}

sections.name: Main Theme Reprise
sections.text: {the call again, now the wandering bells lead it astray, harp arpeggios slowly turning beneath, the strings breathing in a little}

sections.name: Bridge
sections.text: {contrast: the lights crowd closer, an uncanny shift to a C major chord in B minor, the bells circling; then one warm true note glows in key}

sections.name: Main Theme Return
sections.text: {the lantern call returns and this time settles home softly in D major, tender; the last bar drifts straight back into the theme}
styles: seamless loop back to the start of the theme
